scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever causes wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1220-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-06).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) used an ACTUAL meter read rather than an ESTIMATED one, so estimate substitution is not the dominant pattern (E-01).
Manual-read route completion ran at 88% vs a 95% target over 9200 accounts Aug-Sep (E-03), a real but secondary field gap.
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1220-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-06). With tariff changes ruled out (E-02) and ticket response times already within SLA (E-05), and 59% of disputed bills built on an ACTUAL meter read rather than an estimated one (E-01), the best-supported mechanism is a change to billing import validation rules around August that mis-processes bills based on actual reads, producing incorrect bills that drive the dispute surge (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-11: The counts still stand (1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL of 3025 disputed bills), but per E-11 this no longer supports a billing-rule mechanism mis-processing the dominant ACTUAL-read population. E-11 shows the mechanism (valid high-consumption AMI reads rejected on import, REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) explains estimate substitution only within the minority ESTIMATED bucket, so E-01 can no longer be read as evidence that the root-cause mechanism reaches the 59% ACTUAL-read majority.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-04.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against an SLA of 3.0 days (crm-tickets).

F-11.statement: billing-db.import_status_estimated_disputed shows 1184 ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts (firmware v4.2) with import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 (mixed firmware) with NO_READ_RECEIVED.

F-12.statement: billing-db.affected_accounts_v42 lists 1184 distinct accounts, all with bill_read_type=ESTIMATED, firmware=v4.2, import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, spanning 540 distinct ami_read_ts values.

F-13.statement: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts returned 1184 AMI read records (1184 distinct accounts, 540 distinct read timestamps), all bill_read_type=ESTIMATED, firmware=v4.2, import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION.

F-14.statement: The mdms-export.reads_for_accounts query completed as AUTHORITATIVE and COMPLETE, confirming vendor-provisioned MDMS export access is functioning.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily driven by slow or poor-quality ticket responses in CRM, not by actually incorrect bills, so an auto-answer agent would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (around August) is causing bills to be computed or accepted incorrectly, driving disputes.

H-AMI-MDMS-DATA-QUALITY.statement: Degraded AMI read delivery or MDMS validation (vendor side) is causing missing accepted reads, triggering estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reading (contracted via MeterWorks) is failing or incomplete (missed/late routes), causing estimated or substituted bills.

H-SEASONAL-USAGE-SPIKE.statement: Bills issued since August are largely correct, reflecting a legitimate seasonal consumption increase, and the 'wrong bills' premise itself is unverified.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: Billing import validation specifically rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) even when exported from MDMS, forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of the disputed ESTIMATED-read bills.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALE-MISMATCH.statement: BV-17 compares a raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (unit_scaling=none), which may trigger false high-consumption rejections if register values are not in the same scale/units as the historical m3 figures.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) used an ESTIMATED read and 1785 (59%) used an ACTUAL read, so estimate substitution is not the dominant pattern behind disputed bills — most disputes involve bills built on an actual meter read, not a missing/substituted one.

The counts still stand (1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL of 3025 disputed bills), but per E-11 this no longer supports a billing-rule mechanism mis-processing the dominant ACTUAL-read population. E-11 shows the mechanism (valid high-consumption AMI reads rejected on import, REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) explains estimate substitution only within the minority ESTIMATED bucket, so E-01 can no longer be read as evidence that the root-cause mechanism reaches the 59% ACTUAL-read majority.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log shows zero records, indicating no tariff/pricing changes occurred that could independently explain incorrect bills; this rules out a price-change explanation but does not bear on the AMI, field-read, import-rule, response-speed, or seasonal-usage hypotheses already in play.

Field route-log shows manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target for 9200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep, i.e. roughly 12% of manual-read accounts had incomplete/missed routes during the dispute-surge window. This is direct, authoritative evidence of a real (if modest) field-read collection gap, independent of AMI/MDMS, billing-rule, or CRM response-speed factors.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's stakeholder statement that there has been no tariff change this year corroborates the already-recorded authoritative finding (E-02) that no tariff change occurred since August; as an unverified stakeholder claim it adds no new authority but agrees with existing evidence and does not implicate any currently listed hypothesis.

CRM response-time data shows tickets are generally resolved well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets), indicating response speed/quality is not the bottleneck behind the dispute surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul) tickets rising to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep), confirming a roughly 2x jump in dispute volume starting in August — this validates the magnitude/timing of the surge CL-01 describes but says nothing about why bills are wrong.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD, an interested party, claims a 3-reader staffing shortfall since July causes late routes and resulting estimated bills; this is an unverified mechanism offered for the route-completion gap already shown in E-03, not new authoritative data.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 (service contract §4.2) establishes that the utility may request route priority changes but that these are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), formalizing the contractual basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update rather than revealing anything about the billing dispute causal chain.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log's lagging_routes query decomposes the aggregate 88% manual-read completion rate (E-03) into 14 individual routes, each with a distinct completion value (sample: route R-00 at 0.70); this is granular characterization of which routes are behind schedule, not an explanation of why they are behind.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (a stakeholder, not authoritative) states that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471; this is a claim about access status, not evidence about AMI data quality or billing causation, and if true it would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query.

Among disputed bills with an ESTIMATED read (E-01's 1240), MDMS data shows 1184 accounts had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected on import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 truly had no AMI read received. This means estimate substitution for most ESTIMATED-read disputes stems from billing import discarding valid high-consumption reads, not from AMI/MDMS delivery failure.

E-12.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config's validation_rule_changes log confirms rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling=none) was deployed 2026-08-01, matching the dispute-surge timing; the other change (BV-09, 2026-03-02) is a cosmetic label edit unrelated to the surge. This confirms a real billing import rule change occurred around August and ties it specifically to the high-consumption rejection mechanism already seen in E-11, but it does not by itself explain how/if the mechanism reaches the ACTUAL-read majority of disputed bills.

mdms-export.meter_firmware_units shows firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06, before the surge) report raw register values in units of 0.1 m3, while legacy firmware v3.x meters report directly in m3. Since E-11's REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION reads are tagged firmware v4.2 and BV-17 (E-12) compares the raw register value to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none, this confirms a literal ~10x unit-scale mismatch for v4.2 meters: their raw register reading looks 10x higher than true m3 consumption, triggering false high-consumption rejections.

E-14 (billing-db) independently reproduces E-11's split of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills: 1184 (firmware v4.2) rejected on import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and 56 (mixed firmware) NO_READ_RECEIVED. This corroborates, from the billing system's own records rather than only MDMS, that estimate substitution for most ESTIMATED-read disputes stems from import rejection, not AMI delivery failure; it says nothing new about the still-unexplained 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% majority).

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-15 provides the account-level roster underlying the already-confirmed 1184-account REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION cohort (ESTIMATED-read, firmware v4.2) seen aggregated in E-11/E-14, with distinct account_id and ami_read_ts per record, operationally identifying which specific accounts the BV-17 unit-scale mechanism affected rather than revealing any new causal pathway.

E-16.content: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts → 1184 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'ami_read_ts', 'bill_read_type', 'firmware', 'import_status'] | account_id: 1184 distinct values | ami_read_ts: 540 distinct values | bill_read_type: ESTIMATED×1184 | firmware: v4.2×1184 | import_status: REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION×1184 | sample: {"account_id": "AC-10000", "ami_read_ts": "2026-09-01T02:00:00", "bill_read_type": "ESTIMATED", "firmware": "v4.2", "import_status": "REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-16 (mdms-export.reads_for_accounts) independently reproduces, from the AMI/MDMS system itself, the same 1184-account cohort already seen in E-11/E-14/E-15: all ESTIMATED-read, firmware v4.2, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION. It corroborates the confirmed BV-17/unit-scale rejection mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read minority but adds no new information about the still-unexplained 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY).

ER-1.previous_interpretation: Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) used an ESTIMATED read and 1785 (59%) used an ACTUAL read, so estimate substitution is not the dominant pattern behind disputed bills — most disputes involve bills built on an actual meter read, not a missing/substituted one.
ER-1.revised_interpretation: The counts still stand (1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL of 3025 disputed bills), but per E-11 this no longer supports a billing-rule mechanism mis-processing the dominant ACTUAL-read population. E-11 shows the mechanism (valid high-consumption AMI reads rejected on import, REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) explains estimate substitution only within the minority ESTIMATED bucket, so E-01 can no longer be read as evidence that the root-cause mechanism reaches the 59% ACTUAL-read majority.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.question: Did billing import validation rules actually change around August, and if so which rule(s) changed and how do they mis-process actual-read bills?
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the core causal mechanism; if no rule change is found, a different mechanism (not yet in the hypothesis set) must be investigated before any fix is built.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.resolution_path: Query billing-config billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August and correlate timing with the dispute surge (E-06).
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnostic data analysis only; do not build or deploy any automated bill-fix or auto-answer agent until the mechanism is confirmed.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.resolution: Confirmed via E-12: billing import validation rule BV-17 (high-consumption check, raw register vs 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling=none) was deployed 2026-08-01, matching the dispute-surge onset; the only other logged change (BV-09, March) is a cosmetic label edit and unrelated.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.question: Is the route-completion gap (E-03, 88% vs 95% target) actually caused by a 3-reader staffing shortfall since July (SH-FIELD's claim, E-07/CL-03), or by another cause?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.decision_impact: Determines whether the secondary route-completion gap needs a staffing remedy or a different fix, independent of the BV-17 mechanism.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.resolution_path: Review MeterWorks route logs/scheduling records independently of SH-FIELD's self-report to verify a staffing shortfall exists.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.safe_placeholder: Continue monitoring route completion rate without acting on any dispatch route change.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Would AMI read-event records (currently inaccessible, mdms-export ACCESS_PENDING/DEGRADED) reveal any secondary AMI-side contributor to disputed bills if access were granted?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Could qualify the rejected AMI/MDMS hypothesis if vendor access is later granted and data contradicts E-01's current conclusion.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Wait for vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (recovery_decision log notes ACCESS_PENDING) then pull disputed/estimated read events.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI/MDMS as ruled out per E-01 for now; revisit only if vendor access is granted and new data contradicts this.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: Now that MDMS export access is provisioned, E-11 shows AMI read delivery is largely intact for ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts (1184/1240 reads received and exported before cutoff); only 56 accounts had a true missing-read gap, so the AMI-side contributor to disputed bills is minor compared to the billing import rejection mechanism.

U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.question: Do a meaningful share of the 3025 disputed bills reflect genuinely higher seasonal consumption rather than billing computation errors?
U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If a large share of disputes are legitimate consumption increases, the success metric (dispute volume to baseline) is partly the wrong target and a confirmed-error-rate metric is also needed.
U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Compare disputed-bill consumption against prior-year same-period consumption per account in billing-db.
U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report both raw dispute volume and a confirmed-billing-error share; do not assume every dispute is a billing error.

U-DISPUTE-POPULATION-MATCH.question: Does the 3025 disputed-bills population analyzed in billing-db (E-01) correspond to the same tickets driving the CRM dispute-volume surge counted in E-06 (610/590/1180/1260 across Jun-Sep)?
U-DISPUTE-POPULATION-MATCH.decision_impact: If the populations differ, the share of the surge explained by the confirmed BV-17 mechanism may be mis-estimated.
U-DISPUTE-POPULATION-MATCH.resolution_path: Join/compare billing-db disputed_bills records against crm-tickets dispute records for the same window.
U-DISPUTE-POPULATION-MATCH.safe_placeholder: Treat BV-17 as a partial, not complete, explanation of the dispute surge until population linkage is confirmed.

A-DISPUTES-REFLECT-BILLING-ERR.statement: Rising dispute volume reflects actual billing errors rather than legitimate increased consumption, since H-SEASONAL-USAGE-SPIKE remains an unresolved candidate hypothesis.

A-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August is the mechanism producing incorrect bills, though no billing-config rule-change-log evidence has yet been examined to confirm the change itself.

A-FIELD-GAP-SECONDARY.statement: The 88% manual-read route completion gap (E-03) is a real but secondary contributor, not the dominant driver, since disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED (E-01).

A-POPULATION-LINKAGE.statement: The 3025 disputed bills analyzed in billing-db (E-01) are drawn from the same ticket population whose monthly counts are tracked in crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly (E-06).

The best-supported mechanism now confirmed by evidence is that billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), compares a raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling, and because firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out June 2026) report raw readings in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13), BV-17 falsely flags valid high-consumption reads and the import rejects them (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-11) and contributing to the surge. Per ER-1's revision of E-01, this confirmed mechanism does not reach the remaining 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of the 3025 total); their driver is not yet established and is tracked as an open unknown rather than asserted here.

proposal.summary: The problem, as redefined (PD-1@v2) after a key evidence revision, is that CRM dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month since August (E-06), with tariff changes and slow ticket response ruled out (E-02, E-04, E-05). A confirmed mechanism — billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12) comparing unscaled raw register values from firmware v4.2 meters (which report in 0.1 m3, E-13) against m3 history — explains false high-consumption rejections for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-11, E-14-E-16), but does not reach the larger 59% ACTUAL-read majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025, E-01/ER-1), whose driver remains an open unknown. The earlier framing (PD-1@v1) blaming the rule change for the ACTUAL-read majority was invalidated by this new evidence and formally superseded, cascading invalidation/re-evaluation flags through dependent hypotheses, assumptions, remedies, and success criteria (DR-1). The planned release scope (SD-2) was a correlation report on billing data plus a dispute-volume monitor, with no automated bill writes or route-dispatch changes permitted. The release decision is HOLD, not approval: a required data handoff from the AMI/MDMS vendor to billing (H-MDMS-BILL) is flagged with an unresolved semantic mismatch and marked unhealthy/invalid, and the mandatory safety verification (Layer 1, specifically the handoff_delivery_semantic check) failed, so no deliverable was released. Several known limitations and open verification obligations remain regardless of this hold, including unresolved questions about ticket-to-billing linkage, provisional classification of ACTUAL-read disputes, a read-only CRM constraint limiting any future output to a separate report, and the fact that the BV-17 unit-scaling fix cannot be deployed until its own verification obligation (VOB-R-3) is resolved.
